claim_challenged: Maintenance of the complete platform is 800 h/yr (48,000 min), with min_customers 0
challenge: 800 h/yr is about 10.6% of the 7,560 founder hours the model says it takes to build the platform (qualification.csv QUAL-01..05 base). That platform includes an append-only ledger, a grant gate, payment-rail integration, a charity pipeline, three user experiences, a partner API, tenancy and KMS. Planning norms put annual maintenance at 15-25% of build effort, which is 1,130-1,890 h. The workload also includes recurring regulatory change: tax-year changes, Nacha rule changes, PostgreSQL major upgrades gated on Strata support (CNV-ARC-004) and expand/contract migrations per tenant (CNV-ARC-005). Adding these hours has a large effect at zero customers. The engineering residual is now 289 h (headline.csv L,0). At 1,200 h of maintenance it becomes 689 h, all contracted. At 1,500 h it becomes 989 h, which is above hire_threshold_hours 800 (Engine.staffRole), so one engineer is employed before the first customer.
evidence: qualification.csv QUAL-01..05 = 7,560 founder h; Engine.fs staffRole hire rule; headline.csv L,0 contract_hours 289; CNV-ARC-004/005 (U/requirements/PLATFORM-UX-API-AND-ASSURANCE-STANDARDS.md:305,343); the 15-25%-of-build planning norm is industry convention (INFERENCE)
proposed_change: minutes 30000/48000/72000 -> 60000/90000/120000 (1,000/1,500/2,000 h), or derive it as 0.15/0.20/0.25 x qualification founder hours; report the zero-customer engineering hire this triggers
rationale: Maintenance norms (15-25% of build effort) support more than 800 h; AI-assisted maintenance and a modular monolith support less. Reconciled with ADV-O-01 at 500/900/1,800 h, split into keep-qualified (at zero customers) and operating maintenance.

target: inputs/parameters.csv founder_hours_per_new_customer; Engine.fs newCustomers (0 when n=0)
claim_challenged: Sales effort is 160 founder h per new customer, and no sales hours accrue at zero customers
challenge: Two problems. First, the 160 h is charged only for a won customer. Losing pursuits cost about the same, and enterprise win rates of 20-33% mean 3-5 pursuits per win. Second, newCustomers returns 0 at n=0, so the pre-revenue year that must produce the first customer carries no sales hours. Yet the founder is already 100% utilised at zero customers (results.md section 5: 'founder fully utilised' at 0). Every pipeline hour therefore displaces engineering hours, which are contracted at $130/h. At a 25% win rate, the extra lost-deal pursuit is 480 h/yr, which adds $62k to zero-customer cash. Combined with ADV-P-01, the residual exceeds the hire threshold.
evidence: Engine.fs newCustomers: 'if n = 0 then 0.0'; parameters.csv months_to_first_revenue 12 (sales cycles 9-24 months, CHL-013); results.md section 5 founder fully utilised at 0; win-rate range is an assumption
proposed_change: add parameter founder_pipeline_hours 200/480/960 h/yr, charged at every customer count including 0 (lost-deal pursuit at 33%/25%/14% win rates). Alternatively, charge founder_hours_per_new_customer at n=0 with NewCustomers = 1 during the pre-revenue year
rationale: Lost pursuits are real cost of won customers. Folded into hours per won customer via an explicit win rate; pure keep-running zero-customer cost excludes selling, and pursuit of customer 1 is in the go-live capital.

target: model Engine.fs applyCoverage (line ~274: have = employees0 + founder)
claim_challenged: The founder counts as one person in every founder-eligible role for coverage
challenge: The founder is counted as present in every role, including roles where the founder has no hours. In T and F at one customer, the founder's 1,400 h go to management (490 h) and engineering (910 of about 1,529 h, register order). That leaves 0 founder hours in operations, yet COV-OPS (min 2) counts the founder as one of the two people. So the model buys one backup ops analyst ($40k) instead of two ($80k). Preparer/reviewer separation and business-day continuity cannot rest on a person who does no operations work and is also primary on-call and the change author.
evidence: Engine.fs applyCoverage; roles.csv register order (management, engineering, ..., operations); coverage.csv COV-OPS min_people 2; results.md section 4 F,1 shows COV-OPS alternative $40.0k
proposed_change: count the founder toward a role's coverage only when the founder's hours in that role are >0 (better, >=0.25 FTE). Re-run T/F: COV-OPS needs 2 alternatives ($80k) or 1 hire plus 1 alternative. Expect about +$40k in T/F first-customer cash
rationale: Engine flaw confirmed independently by ADV-A-07.
resulting_change: Engine: founder counts only in roles with founder hours

claim_challenged: A contracted secondary on-call retainer at 18k/36k/72k meets two-deep on-call while the founder is primary 52 weeks a year
challenge: (1) There is no price evidence for the retainer. prices-ops.csv LAB-31 says 'No public on-call premium/retainer benchmark found'. (2) Standby alone for an employee averages about $540/week (incident.io survey; recent EU fintech stipends EUR500-1,050/week), which is $28k/yr before any incident hours. A third party adds margin and must keep a named engineer familiar with a bespoke ledger, which takes 100-200 h/yr of shadowing, runbook drills and restore rehearsals at $130/h ($13-26k). (3) The model leaves the founder as 24x7x365 primary. Google's SRE book caps on-call at 25% of time and puts the minimum single-site 24x7 rotation at eight engineers. Two-deep with one founder means 100% primary duty, which is not sustainable for years. Obligations that need prompt response are already defined: an unmatched bank debit is a high-severity incident within 1 h (XDS-BNK-011), and the break-glass tenant notice is due within 1 h (UNB-XIN-IAM-005).
evidence: prices-ops.csv LAB-31 note; https://incident.io/blog/fair-on-call-compensation (avg $540/week); https://sre.google/sre-book/being-on-call/ (minimum 8 single-site; 25% cap); U/requirements/discovery/2026-11-23-cross-industry/15-OPEN-DECISIONS-AND-SCENARIOS.md:125; 03-MISSING-REQUIREMENTS-REGISTER.md:73
proposed_change: alt_annual 18000/36000/72000 -> 45000/70000/120000. The retainer then covers standby, 150 h of familiarisation and drills, and primary cover for at least 8 weeks/yr while the founder is off rota
rationale: incident.io standby benchmark (~$540/week, ~$28k/yr) adopted as base; $70k base would pay for primary cover the founder already provides.

claim_challenged: The founder works 1,400 h/yr (900-1,900) for the DAF business, with no absence deduction
challenge: 1,400 h is 70% of a 2,000-h work year, net of all other Echelon Foundry work. In those hours the founder is CEO, the only salesperson, the lead engineer and change author, primary on-call, the designated security officer (the EXP-SEC-09 alternative) and compliance owner. No leave, sickness or conference time is deducted. Typical US leave plus sickness is 150-250 h/yr. The tornado already shows this is the largest single swing in first-customer cash (+/-$107k), and the base sits at the favourable end. A one-founder vendor is also a key-person risk that buyers price in (PRI-02 remaining uncertainty: 'whether buyers accept a one-founder vendor').
evidence: results.md section 14 tornado PAR:founder_hours_per_year swing $107.1k; parameters.csv basis 'Not a commitment'; prior-estimates.csv PRI-02
proposed_change: 900/1400/1900 -> 700/1100/1600, with an explicit 200 h absence deduction. Each -300 h adds about $39k cash at every customer count (contracted engineering at $130/h)
rationale: Absence deduction accepted; 700 h base not evidenced.

target: outputs/capital.csv (Analysis.capitalFor PreRevenueBurn = months x zero-customer cash); inputs/coverage.csv trigger_customers 1; inputs/activities.csv ACT-PLT-07 min_customers 1
claim_challenged: Controls, coverage and SOC evidence start with the first customer
challenge: Institutional buyers expect a SOC 2 Type II report. A Type II covers an observation period (typically 3-12 months) in which the controls must actually operate. That means the controls run before the first customer: non-author change approval (CNV-PLT-010 has no activation gate beyond release scope), two-person break-glass, on-call and access reviews. Evidence collection also runs, because SOC2-008 forbids marking a control operating without observed evidence. The model costs none of this pre-revenue. PreRevenueBurn uses zero-customer cash, which has no coverage, no ACT-PLT-07 and no insurance. VAL-02 also runs a parallel pilot on a partner's real customer data while EXP-INS-01 is untriggered.
evidence: U/requirements/governance/SOC2-CONTROLS-EVIDENCE-AND-ENTERPRISE-DIRECTIVE.md SOC2-008/SOC2-023; PLATFORM-UX-API-AND-ASSURANCE-STANDARDS.md:312 (CNV-PLT-010 activation gate: none beyond release scope); prices-ops.csv AUD-05/AUD-06; qualification.csv VAL-02
proposed_change: add parameter soc2_observation_months 3/6/12. Pre-revenue capital should carry COV-CHG, COV-BRK and COV-ONC alternatives, ACT-PLT-07 hours and EXP-INS-01 for that window. Base 6 months adds about (52k+12k+36k+17.6k+3k)/2, roughly $60k, to capital before first revenue
rationale: SOC 2 observation, coverage and insurance must operate at go-live.
resulting_change: go_live_lead_months 3/6/12 of first-customer run-rate in capital

claim_challenged: Two contracted non-author reviewers at 13k/26k/50k each (100-300 h/yr) satisfy CNV-PLT-010
challenge: CNV-PLT-010 requires two non-author approvers on every control-module change and has no emergency exception. An emergency fix to the ledger, holds or dispatch during a Sev-1 needs two approvers reachable within the RTO (C0 RTO <=4 h). A review retainer priced on hours does not buy 24x7 availability. Reviewers able to judge fund-accounting ledger code are also scarcer than generic contract engineers, so priced at the $130/h engineering rate rather than $89 SRE (LAB-31). Each release must also send each sponsor a notice listing changed control modules, which is unmodelled author time.
evidence: PLATFORM-UX-API-AND-ASSURANCE-STANDARDS.md:312; architecture-obligations.md section 2 (C0 RPO 0, RTO <=4 h)
proposed_change: alt_annual 13000/26000/50000 -> 20000/40000/70000 per reviewer, with an emergency-availability clause (4 h response). Alternatively, require that one reviewer is the COV-ONC secondary and price that person's overlap. Add 0.25 h per release per sponsor for the notice in ACT-PLT-03
rationale: Emergency availability accepted; workload is ~40 h per reviewer (ADV-O-03), so retainer priced on workload plus availability clause.

claim_challenged: Coverage is evaluated with the founder always available
challenge: Take a correlated day: 31 December, a database incident, and the founder ill or travelling. That day needs a primary and a backup on-call responder, two-person break-glass activation (sealed credentials, expires in 4 h, tenant notified within 1 h, UNB-XIN-IAM-005), and two non-author approvers for any control-module fix. That is at least three or four qualified non-founder people at once. The modelled retainers supply one on-call secondary and two reviewers who are not on call. Unbound's own scenario XDS-ADV-007 is 'break-glass during a 31 December database outage'. On revenue, December holds 19.5% of grants.
evidence: U/requirements/discovery/2026-11-23-cross-industry/15-OPEN-DECISIONS-AND-SCENARIOS.md:315 (XDS-ADV-007); 03-MISSING-REQUIREMENTS-REGISTER.md:73 (UNB-XIN-IAM-005); architecture-obligations.md section 2 December
proposed_change: add coverage rule COV-ABS: 'founder unavailable', models L W T F, trigger 1, min_people 3 non-founder engineering-qualified persons reachable 24x7, alt_allowed Y, alt_annual 15000/30000/60000 (tertiary responder retainer). Alternatively, evaluate all coverage rules with founder = 0 persons for 8 weeks/yr and pro-rate
rationale: Tier 1 already guarantees non-founder incident and approval coverage (secondary on-call, two reviewers). A 3-4 person 24x7 non-founder bench is the tier-2 COV-ONC24 rule; Unbound sets no contractual SLA until pilot evidence (CNV-ARC-001).

target: inputs/activities.csv ACT-GRT-01 ACT-PAY-01 ACT-CHV-01 ACT-PFL-01 ACT-CTR-01 ACT-CNT-01 (T/F); Engine staffing on annual hours
claim_challenged: Operations staffing is sized on annual hours / 1,600
challenge: Grant- and contribution-driven exception work is concentrated. December carries 19.5% of grants (UNB-AVL-013) against an average month of 8.3%, and year-end contributions peak at the same time, during the heaviest leave period. At F with 10 customers, grant-driven ops hours are about 3,150 h/yr (workload.csv). December alone is about 615 h against a 262 h average month, an excess of about 350 h, plus a contribution surge. Exception queues have sponsor-set business-day deadlines (COV-OPS basis), so surge capacity must be pre-contracted and trained.

proposed_change: add parameter peak_month_share 0.195 (0.15-0.25) for grant/contribution-driven activities. Size T/F operations to peak-month hours, or add surge contract hours = (peak - average month) x 1.25 premium rate. Expect about +$40-55k/yr at F10
rationale: December concentration accepted; annual hours already include December volume, so only surge coordination and premium are added.

claim_challenged: Licensing, white-label, T and F customers onboard in 300 h with no data migration
challenge: Every sponsor buying L, W, T or F already administers DAFs in a legacy system. Its funds, balances, four-date contribution history, grant history and successor designations must be converted and reconciled before go-live (the Transitus reconciliation-gated cutover). The model costs migration only in model M, so a first L or F customer needs either an M project, which is uncosted inside L/F and competes for the same founder and contractor hours, or no migration at all, which is not credible. The 300 h onboarding also assumes templates that do not exist for customers 1-2.
evidence: activities.csv ACT-MIG-01 'Source-system extraction, mapping, rehearsal and reconciliation-gated cutover' ef_models M; ACT-IMP-01 18,000 min vs conventional 36,000
proposed_change: add L W T F to ACT-MIG-01/02 ef_models, or add a mandatory coupling in which each new L/W/T/F customer also consumes ACT-MIG hours (150 h + 2 min/account) whether billed or not. Set ACT-IMP-01 minutes for the first two customers to 12000/24000/36000
rationale: Migration is model M sold separately or performed by the sponsor; sponsor-side migration work and first-customer onboarding without templates are added.

claim_challenged: Under licensing a SOC 1 is contract-demanding only, and auditor support is 20 h per customer
challenge: Under licensing, Unbound hosts the sponsor's DAF subledger of record. Under AU-C 402 the sponsor's auditor must understand and, where it relies on them, test the service organization's controls. Without a SOC 1 Type 2, the auditor tests ITGCs (access, change, operations) and samples transactions directly, separately for each sponsor. Twenty hours of walkthroughs, PBC requests and sample pulls per auditor-year is light. A SOC 1 is therefore contract-typical once more than a few sponsors rely on the ledger.
evidence: AICPA AU-C 402 (user auditor's consideration of a service organization); architecture-obligations.md section 4 ('SOC 1 Type 2 applies when a user auditor relies on Unbound's controls'); expenses.csv EXP-SEC-08
proposed_change: EXP-SEC-08 obligation contract-demanding -> contract-typical for L/W, OR ACT-AUD-02 minutes 600/1200/2400 -> 1500/3000/6000 when no SOC 1 is held (switch to the SOC 1 path when cheaper)
rationale: Under licensing Unbound holds the ledger of record; SOC 1 becomes contract-typical from the third customer, below which auditor walkthroughs are cheaper.

claim_challenged: Engineering after qualification is only maintenance, security, pipelines and customer-specific fixes
challenge: No hours are budgeted for product enhancement. That covers features prospects require in procurement (SSO and SCIM, reporting, integrations with GL and CRM, statement formats) and competitive parity with incumbent DAF systems. ACT-PLT-11 covers only 'customer-requested fixes'. Because the founder is fully utilised at zero customers, the model implicitly freezes the product at qualification for the whole sales cycle (12-24 months).
evidence: activities.csv ACT-PLT-10/11 definitions; results.md section 5 founder fully utilised at 0

rationale: Enhancement to win and retain customers is discretionary in a zero-based minimum (no obligation, workload or capacity trigger). Its cost is reported as a sensitivity (800 h ~ $96k/yr at contract rates) in report 05.

claim_challenged: Base case: first employee at 4 customers (L) and 2 (F)
challenge: The model's own Monte Carlo puts the median first employee at 1 customer for both L and F, and the ρ=0.5 run puts L's P90 at 6. The deterministic base sits at the optimistic end of the model's own distribution. That happens because the hire threshold is a cliff, and several base inputs (founder hours, maintenance, retainer prices) sit near it. The correlated run uses ρ=0.5 only among adverse draws. It does not model the joint December, incident and founder-absence event.

resulting_change: Answers headline Monte Carlo P50/P90 next to the mode case

claim_challenged: A SOC 2 Type II costs 7k/12k/45k
challenge: The base uses micro-company medians (AUD-01 $9k, 'before scoping'). This system handles grant payment instructions and a ledger, so its scope will likely add Availability, Processing Integrity and Confidentiality to Security. It also has several subservice organizations and contracted personnel. First-year Type II fees for small and mid-size companies run $12-20k (AUD-05) and the specialist band is $15-45k (AUD-03). Year-two renewals run 60-100% of year one (AUD-10).
evidence: prices-ops.csv AUD-01, AUD-03, AUD-05, AUD-06 (first-year all-in $25-50k), AUD-10
rationale: Survey median for 1-10 staff is $9k (AUD-01); $12k base already sits above it; high kept at $45k.

claim_challenged: Tier 1 insurance is $2M E&O/cyber (uplift 1.5k/3.6k/5.4k). Crime under licensing is contract-demanding
challenge: (1) INS-10 notes that fintech and fund-flow exposure pushes premiums toward the high end, and INS-11 runs $3-12k for $2M. A pre-revenue single-founder platform that dispatches payment instructions will not price at the median. (2) Under L and W, the dispatch module produces payment instructions, so a compromised platform can redirect grants (ACT-FRD-01 exists for this reason). Sponsors' risk teams commonly require vendor crime or social-engineering cover. (3) Market practice for small vendors is $2-5M (INS-25), universities require $5M (INS-26) and bank partners $3-5M (INS-27). The anchor and national profiles (L, XL) fall in this group.
evidence: prices-ops.csv INS-10, INS-11, INS-25, INS-26, INS-27
proposed_change: EXP-INS-02 amount 1500/3600/5400 -> 3000/6000/9000; EXP-INS-05 obligation contract-demanding -> contract-typical; apply EXP-INS-03 at tier 1 whenever the mix includes an L or XL profile
rationale: Micro-SaaS medians understate fintech premiums (also ADV-A-20).
resulting_change: EXP-INS-01 2/4/10k; EXP-INS-02 2/4.5/9k; crime under licensing stays tier 2 (EF never moves money)

claim_challenged: Counsel is $5k per new customer and $10k/yr for open legal questions
challenge: At the $355/h average outside-counsel rate (LAB-33), $5k is 14 h. Negotiating an MSA, DPA, insurance schedule and TPSP terms with an institution's counsel, or a bank's, typically takes 20-40 h. EXP-COR-04's $10k is 28 h to resolve at least four open questions (TPSP role under Nacha, source rights, privacy, IP assignment) plus breach-notification duties. FTC Safeguards applicability is still 'uncertain' (XRA-007), and state breach-notification law applies.

rationale: Annual counsel raised less than proposed because template work is in qualification (ADV-O-17).

claim_challenged: Security operations take 200 h/yr
challenge: The obligations in scope are: quarterly access recertification for privileged and workforce roles, including bank and custodian signer registers, with auto-suspension (UNB-XIN-IAM-004); SOC2-010 through SOC2-016 (identity lifecycle, monitoring, vulnerability and dependency programs); key rotation evidence; and joiner/leaver handling for at least 4-6 contractors, with revocation within 1 h on termination. Bottom-up: log review at 15 min per business day is 62 h, patching and dependencies 104 h, vulnerability triage 52 h, access reviews 4 x 8 h = 32 h, key rotation 16 h, contractor lifecycle and training 30 h. Total about 300 h.
evidence: U/requirements/discovery/2026-11-23-cross-industry/03-MISSING-REQUIREMENTS-REGISTER.md:118 (UNB-XIN-IAM-004); SOC2 directive SOC2-010..016; 10-ORGANIZATIONAL-AND-STAFFING-MODELS.md:166
rationale: Midpoint between 300 h (P) and 90 h (O) proposals is the current 200 h base; range 100-400 h retained.

claim_challenged: Regional recovery from backup in about 24 h is acceptable at tier 1, and DR tests take 32 h/yr
challenge: The candidate C0 objective (ledger, holds, approvals) is RTO <=4 h. CNV-ARC-001 lets cross-region recovery declare a nonzero RPO but grants no RTO relief. A regional outage with only cross-region backup copies (about 24 h) breaches C0. Restore tests must cover each of five data classes and each isolation profile annually (RR-UNB-RES-003-r1), while SPW-137 says semi-annual drills. The base of two drills at 16 h each does not cover five classes plus a cross-region rehearsal. Either recovery must run without the founder, or the founder is the RTO single point of failure.
evidence: architecture-obligations.md section 2 (C0 RPO 0 RTO <=4 h; restore per class; SPW-137 semi-annual); expenses.csv EXP-INF-03 alternative text
proposed_change: EXP-INF-03 obligation contract-demanding -> contract-typical (+$1.3k/yr). Alternatively, state in results that tier 1 does not meet C0 RTO in a regional outage. ACT-PLT-05 minutes 480/960/1920 -> 960/1920/3840 at rate 2, including one cross-region restore rehearsal run by the non-founder secondary
rationale: CNV-ARC-001 lets cross-region recovery declare a nonzero RPO; the C0 4 h RTO is met in-region by the synchronous standby.

claim_challenged: Vendor assurance and policy upkeep take 40 h/yr
challenge: SOC2-013 and CNV-GOV-002 require an inventory and annual due diligence for critical services and subservice organizations. That includes reviewing their SOC reports and mapping complementary user entity controls. Critical vendors here are the cloud provider, AI provider, email, paging, compliance platform, help desk, code host, KMS, three retainer firms, pen tester and charity data: about 8 critical at 3 h each and 8 others at 1 h, roughly 32 h. On top of that come annual review of about 15-20 SOC 2 policies (20-40 h) and the SOC2-024 owner attestations. All of this is founder-held, so it displaces founder hours.
evidence: SOC2 directive SOC2-013, SOC2-024; architecture-obligations.md section 4 (CNV-GOV-002 annual)
rationale: Vendor assurance and policy upkeep raised.

claim_challenged: Platform incidents run 12/yr at 4 h each (48 h)
challenge: New platforms have their highest incident rates in years 1-2. Bank-feed and payment-file integrations add failure modes, and an unmatched debit is a high-severity incident within 1 h. Each incident needs documented detection, triage, containment, communication and lessons learned (SOC2-026), and sponsor notification where tenant data is touched. Four hours including the postmortem is lean.
evidence: SOC2 directive SOC2-026; 15-OPEN-DECISIONS-AND-SCENARIOS.md:125 (XDS-BNK-011)
proposed_change: rate 6/12/30 -> 12/24/48 for the first two operating years; minutes 120/240/600 -> 180/360/720
rationale: Early operating years see more incidents.

target: inputs/activities.csv (missing AI evaluation and model-change revalidation)

Provider model retirements arrive every 12-18 months and force re-evaluation of dossier and extraction prompts against the deterministic sections, with adversarial tests and evidence. No activity covers this. PRI-01 listed 'AI evaluation and governance' as a cost, and the zero-based model dropped it entirely rather than resizing it.

claim_challenged: No vendor-continuity cost
challenge: Unbound's failure catalogue handles vendor insolvency through an escrowed export package and schema, plus read-only continuity (XFC-SAS-011). Institutions buying from a one-founder vendor routinely ask for source or SaaS escrow as key-person mitigation. List prices are about $1.6-2.2k/yr plus setup and optional verification. SaaS escrow that includes a runnable environment costs more.

rationale: Escrow is a demanding-buyer requirement, not typical.

claim_challenged: Up to 799 h/yr of bespoke-platform engineering can be bought at $130/h with no overhead
challenge: Several part-time contractors touch control-relevant code: residual engineering, the on-call secondary and two reviewers. Each needs background screening, access provisioning and revocation, NDA and IP assignment (still a counsel TODO), and familiarisation with the codebase. When a contractor turns over, the familiarisation cost recurs. None of this overhead appears in the contract hours.

rationale: Contractor familiarisation folded into the contract rate.

claim_challenged: Tier-2 sponsor support is 50 contacts/customer-yr x 30 min
challenge: The steady-state rate is generous against the benchmarks: BEN-06 gives 0.3-1.0 tickets per customer per month, or 4-12 a year. So it is not understated. What is missing is go-live hypercare. Ticket volume in the first 60-90 days after go-live typically runs several times steady state, and contract response objectives (CNV-PLT-005: acknowledge in 2 business days) apply from day one.
evidence: prices-ops.csv BEN-06, BEN-07; PLATFORM-UX-API-AND-ASSURANCE-STANDARDS.md CNV-PLT-005
proposed_change: keep the ACT-SUP-02 rate. Add ACT-IMP-03 'Go-live hypercare', per_new_customer, minutes 2400/4800/9600 split support/engineering, L W T F
rationale: Hypercare after go-live is real work.

claim_challenged: Workspace and identity at $550/yr cover access security
challenge: Cyber insurers' underwriting questionnaires and SOC 2 auditors expect endpoint protection (EDR) and device management on every device with production access, including contractors' devices. LAB-30 gives managed EDR at about $9-15 per endpoint per month. For 6-10 endpoints that is $0.7-1.8k/yr, plus MDM.
evidence: prices-ops.csv LAB-30; SOC2 directive SOC2-010/SOC2-012
proposed_change: add EXP-SEC-10 'Endpoint protection and device management', operational-mandatory, trigger customers 1, amount 700/1500/3000
rationale: Devices with production access need endpoint protection.

claim_challenged: 800 h/yr fixed maintenance (48,000 min base), the largest fixed engineering load, active from 0 customers

evidence: activities.csv ACT-PLT-10 minutes 30000/48000/72000 and conventional_minutes 48000 (identical); EXP-AI-02 purpose 'Coding and analysis assistants for maintenance'; architecture-obligations.md s1 (single managed cluster, no broker in release 1); tornado: ACT-PLT-10 swing $81.1k on L first-customer cash. claim_challenged: Coverage persons counted = employees + founder only; contracted hours never count as a distinct qualified person
challenge: At L/1 customer the model already buys ~620 contract engineering hours (a named contractor working ~40% time) and then additionally buys $52k of reviewers, $12k break-glass holder and $36k secondary on-call as if no second engineer existed. A contractor with ~600 h/yr of production work is exactly the person who can be secondary on-call, second break-glass activator and one non-author approver; the requirement (CNV-PLT-010) asks for distinct approvers, not employees, and ORG-R14 states the on-call role can_be_fractional=Y and can_be_outsourced=Y. Same pattern in T/F: ~300 contracted operations hours plus a $40k COV-OPS backup retainer.
evidence: Engine.fs applyCoverage: have = employees0 + (founder?1:0); roles.jsonl:14 ORG-R14 can_be_fractional Y, can_be_outsourced Y; headline.csv L,1: labor_cash $234.5k of which coverage alternatives $100k and contract hours 1,124; workload.csv engineering fixed ~1,529 h at 1 customer.

At L/1 this removes the COV-BRK and COV-ONC alternatives and one of two COV-CHG reviewers: about -$65k to -$75k first-customer cash (T/F: about -$95k to -$105k incl. COV-OPS).

claim_challenged: $26k/yr per reviewer (~200 h at $130) and two reviewers = $52k/yr at the first customer
challenge: Workload arithmetic from the model's own inputs: ACT-PLT-03 assumes 100 changes/yr; CNV-PLT-010 binds only changes to control-relevant modules (gate, ledger, reservations, holds, authority, dispatch), plausibly <=50% of changes. 50 changes x 2 reviewers x 45 min = 75 reviewer-hours/yr = ~$9.8k at $130 for both reviewers, not $52k. AI cannot be an approver (UNB-AI-STD-003: agents may not self-approve) but AI pre-review legitimately shortens human review minutes. A retainer with a small monthly minimum plus per-review hourly billing fits; a partner's engineers (W) could serve as an in-kind independent approver under contract.
evidence: unbound/requirements/PLATFORM-UX-API-AND-ASSURANCE-STANDARDS.md:312 CNV-PLT-010 ('Modules tagged control-relevant ... SHALL require two approvers on every change, neither the author'); :45 UNB-AI-STD-003; activities.csv ACT-PLT-03 rate 50/100/200 x 40 min; coverage.csv COV-CHG alt 13000/26000/50000; tornado COV-CHG swing $74k.

claim_challenged: A $36k/yr contracted secondary on-call is needed from the first customer

The model's own incident load is 12 incidents x 4 h = 48 h/yr (ACT-PLT-01). $36k for 48 incident-hours is ~$750 per incident-hour. Two-deep comes from an adversarial review cited in ORG-R14, not a contract. For a pilot-stage sponsor with capability SLOs, founder primary plus pay-per-incident contractor (LAB-31 contract SRE $49-150/h) with a modest standby fee is adequate, and degraded-mode design (UNB-AVL-011: refuse new work, status page; holds never queued) limits harm from a slower response.
evidence: unbound/requirements/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md XID-SAS-004; architecture-obligations.md s2 and s8; roles.jsonl:14 (minimum_count sourced to review-arch-econ.md); prices-ops.csv LAB-31 ('No public on-call premium/retainer benchmark found'); activities.csv ACT-PLT-01 12 x 240 min.

With ADV-O-02 it is met by the contracted engineer at no extra alternative.

target: Zero-customer state (ACT-PLT-04/05/09/13 and PLT-10 at min_customers 0)

claim_challenged: 200 h/yr (12,000 min) fixed

target: roles.csv hire_threshold_hours (engineering 800; operations 800; compliance 800; implementation 800; support 900)
claim_challenged: Residual work above 800 h is employed rather than contracted
challenge: The threshold is not cost-minimising. At the model's own prices an engineering employee costs $196.5k vs residual contract hours at $130: break-even = 196,503/130 = 1,511 h. Hiring at 801 h costs $196.5k against $104k contracted (+$92k). Equivalent break-evens: implementation 140,000/110 = 1,273 h; operations 120,925/85 = 1,423 h; compliance 116,662/110 = 1,060 h; support 65,167/50 = 1,303 h. The rule converts a contracting decision into a conventional headcount decision.

claim_challenged: Contract engineering at $90/$130/$200 per hour
challenge: The model's own survey gives contract SRE/DevOps at $49/$89/$150 (LAB-31). target: ACT-IMP-01 Customer onboarding (300 h per new customer)
claim_challenged: Flat 18,000 min per new customer for every profile, with no learning curve

Data migration is excluded (model M carries it). The same 300 h is charged for a 60-account XS foundation as for a 6,000-account L sponsor, and for customer #10 as for #1. A declarative tenant manifest (policy, fee, templates, bank file format, GL export mapping) plus scripted parallel-run comparison should take a repeat XS/S onboarding to ~100-150 h. First-of-kind onboarding may legitimately stay ~300 h.

claim_challenged: $40k/yr contracted backup operations analyst at the first customer

Business-day continuity (exceptions within sponsor-set business days, complaint acknowledgment in 2 business days, CNV-PLT-005) at ~300 h/yr workload (~1.2 h/business day) is met by a second analyst on call-off at hourly rates.

claim_challenged: At 1-4 customers the model onboards and sells one new customer every year (max 1, round(n x 0.3))

This is growth investment, not operating cost; it inflates run-rate, break-even customer counts and the 'can the first customer finance the next' table (s11), which then double-counts the next customer's acquisition.

claim_challenged: Fixed per-customer close and reporting effort irrespective of sponsor size

On a single continuously reconciled ledger, close preparation is a review of already-matched balances; Schedule D/990 DAF inputs are marked deterministic=Y. claim_challenged: A $35k SOC 1 Type II plus 120 h is a contract-typical cost of the first T customer
challenge: CNV-GOV-001 triggers SOC 1 Type 2 planning when the sponsor's user auditor states an intent to rely on platform controls (planned-approach record); for T (unlike the staffed F offer) that is not automatic. target: ACT-PLT-09 charity and sanctions data pipeline stewardship (200 h)
claim_challenged: 200 h/yr fixed for connectors to free federal files
challenge: The sources (EO BMF, Pub 78, revocation, 990-N, 990 e-file index, OFAC SLS) are stable published formats; freshness alarms and archive are automated. Upkeep is format-change fixes (a few per year) and alarm response. Phase II's 400 h was a conventional single-sponsor estimate; halving it once is not a zero-based derivation.

claim_challenged: 50 tickets per customer-year, same for L, W, T, F

challenge: Unbound resolved that no sponsor model offers live phone channels at release 1: 'None; async + scheduled callback' (XID-SVC-005). The cost is a conventional channel the requirements exclude.

challenge: The row lists self-service and proactive status as the prevention mechanisms and ai_assist=Y, yet 80% of contacts reach a human. target: ACT-PLT-11 customer-specific maintenance (40 h per customer) and ACT-PLT-02
claim_challenged: 40 h/yr per customer of integrations, configuration defects and customer-requested fixes
challenge: A multi-tenant platform with schema-per-tenant and declarative configuration should carry no per-customer code; configuration defects are platform defects (already in PLT-10) and configuration changes are ACT-IMP-02. 40 h/customer is a conventional single-tenant customisation allowance.

target: Small tooling and insurance lines (EXP-SUP-01, EXP-INF-12, EXP-INS-07, EXP-INS-02)
claim_challenged: Help desk $600, paging/status $700, GL $500 and $2M E&O uplift $3.6k from customer 1
challenge: Each has a free or bundled alternative in the package's own surveys: Workspace shared inbox (SUP-06) until >2 support seats; Grafana Cloud Free on-call for 3 users; GL is inside the startup GL+E&O+cyber bundle (INS-07 $2-4k) and Vouch GL median is $180 (INS-22); $1M limits are negotiable with XS/S community foundations under L/W where EF never moves money (INS-25 range starts at $2M for institutional buyers, so keep uplift for M/L/XL profiles).
evidence: prices-ops.csv SUP-06, INS-07, INS-22, INS-25; prices-infra.csv Grafana Cloud Free; expenses.csv alternatives on each row.
proposed_change: EXP-SUP-01 0/0/2000 until customers>=5; EXP-INF-12 0/300/1400; EXP-INS-07 0/200/1000; EXP-INS-02 trigger on first M-or-larger profile. ~-$2k to -$5k/yr.
rationale: Minor; lines kept for completeness.

claim_challenged: $5k/yr forensic retainer for demanding contracts
challenge: The package's own survey notes cyber insurers provide panel IR firms and advises checking the policy before buying a retainer; EXP-INS-01 is always bought from customer 1.
evidence: prices-ops.csv LAB-32 notes; expenses.csv EXP-IR-01 'Often available through the cyber insurer's panel at no extra cost'.
proposed_change: EXP-IR-01 amount 0/0/15000 (base: insurer panel).
rationale: Insurer breach panels usually provide incident response.

target: QUAL-06 independent review of control modules before launch ($40k cash)
claim_challenged: Pre-launch non-author review of control modules costs $20k/$40k/$80k
challenge: At $130/h, $40k is ~300 reviewer hours. Control modules (gate, ledger, reservations, holds, authority, dispatch) in a modular monolith are plausibly 10-20k lines; at 200-400 reviewed lines per hour that is 25-100 h per reviewer x 2 reviewers = 50-200 h ($6.5k-26k). AI pre-review and property tests reduce human minutes but not the approver requirement.
evidence: qualification.csv QUAL-06; CNV-PLT-010; roles.csv engineering contract $130.
proposed_change: QUAL-06 cash 10000/25000/60000. Capital before first revenue -$15k (base).
rationale: Control-module review cash reduced.

claim_challenged: Small community foundations have 20% more exceptions per transaction
challenge: No source supports a size-related exception uplift; the price survey states no public data on DAF exception rates exists (BEN-09). The base human shares already embed the measured 10.9% routing from the synthetic year. The uplift raises T/F operations hours for the first customers specifically (mix starts with S).
evidence: profiles.csv exception_rate base 1.2 (XS, S) vs 1.0 (M, L, XL); prices-ops.csv BEN-09; architecture-obligations.md s5 (10.9% measured).
proposed_change: exception_rate 0.6/1.0/2.5 for XS and S (keep the wide range, drop the base uplift).
rationale: No evidence for an exception uplift at small sponsors.

target: Model F staffing (operations role, ACT-GRT-01, ACT-PAY-01 etc.)
claim_challenged: Echelon Foundry employs/contracts operations analysts in F although the sponsor decides everything
challenge: Checked and NOT challenged in substance: F is by definition the staffed offer (OD-M-08) and preparation of exceptions, close and reporting is EF work even though every decision stays with the sponsor (CNV-GOV-004; ACT-GRT-02, REC-03, PAY-02 correctly borne by the sponsor). The overstatement is in the mechanism and sizing (ADV-O-02, -10, -16, -23), not the existence of the role. If the sponsor's own staff prepare, the offer is T, not F.
evidence: activities.csv sponsor-borne rows ACT-GRT-02, ACT-REC-03, ACT-PAY-02; architecture-obligations.md s3 (CNV-GOV-004, UNB-CDD-CMF-002 release 1 runs with no Unbound staff in sponsor workflows).
proposed_change: No change to role existence; apply the sizing changes above. Consider stating that F should not be offered at release 1 given UNB-CDD-CMF-002.
rationale: F needs EF operations by definition; UNB-CDD-CMF-002 (no Unbound staff in sponsor workflows in release 1) means F is not a release-1 offer.

claim_challenged: Capital before first revenue is $118k-$166k (L/W/T, base, excl. qualification) and the $1.0-1.5M Phase II pilot budget is revised to $133k
challenge: Capital stops at first invoice + 1 month of working capital, but the self-financing table shows the business losing money for years after first revenue (L -$270k at 1 customer, negative until 7; W/T negative until 16; C until 29). At one new customer per year the cumulative base-case deficit to sustained self-financing is L $1.06M, W $2.00M, T $2.24M, C $1.97M, F $0.31M (scratch run). Prior PRI-08 is defined as capital 'to the first referenceable paying customer... over 12-24 months' including build; the comparable excludes both build cash and post-revenue losses, so the claimed 85-90% reduction is not like-for-like. On a like-for-like basis the L figure (~$1.2M with qualification cash) confirms the prior instead of overturning it.
evidence: explore2.fsx: cumulative negative surplus over n=1..last-negative using evaluate baseSc n; self-financing.csv; prior-estimates.csv PRI-08 original_assumptions
proposed_change: Add a 'capital to self-financing' measure: sum of max(0, EfCash-Revenue) along a stated growth path (e.g. new_customer_share or 1/yr) until surplus stays >=0, plus qCash + readiness + WC; use it (not ExcludingQualification) as the PRI-08 comparable and in the s10 headline
rationale: Capital now follows a growth path to self-sustaining operation; the like-for-like pilot comparison supports the prior range in the base case.

claim_challenged: Break-even: L 7 customers, T 12, W 17, F 2 customers at 20 bps, F 7 at 10 bps
challenge: Counts are an artefact of the pattern order. Customer 7 in 'mixed' is the L profile (6,000 accounts, about half of all accounts in the 10-customer cycle) and customer 2 is an M profile (1,500 accounts, $270M AUA); every model's break-even lands on those positions. Same inputs with other mixes: small (all S) L 34, W/T never, F@10bps never, F@20bps 6; tiny: all never; anchor: L 2, F@20bps 1, F@10bps 1. At n=7 'mixed' carries 1,423 accounts/customer vs the cycle mean 1,182, so the reported counts are biased low.
evidence: explore.fsx BE runs per mix (cashFirst/sustained/loaded); mixes.csv pattern S M S XS M S L S M XS
proposed_change: Report break-even primarily in accounts and AUA (portfolio scale) and as a count only for (a) the expected customer (cycle-average profile, fractional) and (b) the min/max over rotations of the pattern; show all mixes side by side in s7 rather than 'mixed' only
rationale: Break-even, self-financing and capital are reported for every mix.

claim_challenged: T cash break-even at 12 customers (reference price)
challenge: firstWhere returns the first n where revenue >= cost, not the point after which it stays there. T crosses at 12 then falls back below cost (step hires) and is only sustained from 17. Self-financing shows the same non-monotonicity (T surplus -$758 at 9, -$52k at 10).
evidence: explore.fsx: mixed T cashFirst=12 sustained30=17; self-financing.csv T row
proposed_change: Define break-even as the smallest n such that rev>=cost for all k in [n, n+30] (or to scanLimit); report both first-crossing and sustained
rationale: Break-even must persist.

target: Analysis.fs:16-28 (headline uses atLevel Base); Sampling.fs:10-15; results.md s1/s13
claim_challenged: Headline tables at 'base' are the central estimate
challenge: Base is the mode of right-skewed triangular ranges (e.g. PLT-10 30k/48k/72k min, SEC-04 7k/12k/45k), so base sits below the independent Monte Carlo P10: L first-customer cash base $306k vs P10 $329k / P50 $373k; F $432k vs P10 $468k / P50 $517k; L zero-customer $44.6k vs P50 $70k. Mean-of-range inputs give L1 $384k, F10 $1.45M vs $1.17M (+24%). First employee: base 4 customers for L, but 68% of draws hire an engineer with the first customer (9% at zero customers). Calling these figures 'base' overstates confidence.
evidence: monte-carlo.csv vs headline.csv; explore2.fsx mean-input realisation and MC share of employees at n=1 (L 0.68, F 0.68)
proposed_change: Headline P50 (or the mean-input case) next to base and state the percentile of the base case; or re-centre ranges so base = median. Reword the staffing-threshold text to 'first employee at 1 customer in most draws'
rationale: See ADV-P-13.

claim_challenged: Steady-state cost at 1-2 customers and single-customer break-even AUA
challenge: max 1.0 (round(n*0.3)) puts a full new-customer onboarding into every year at n=1..4 (implementation 300-360 h, contract counsel $5k, 160 founder sales hours displacing contract engineering). At n=1 that is $58.8k/yr of L's $306k (19%) and F's $432k (14%); at n=2 it is $26.5k more than the fractional 0.6. A single customer cannot be both steady state and onboarding a new customer every year. Single-customer break-even AUA carries the same $58.8k (about $29M of AUA at 20 bps).
evidence: explore.fsx steady-state: L n=1 306,035 vs 247,235 with NewCustomers=0; n=2 321,288 vs 294,768 at 0.6
proposed_change: Split year-1 and steady state: steady-state tables use NewCustomers = n*new_customer_share (fractional, no floor); onboarding of customer 1 goes into capital/readiness (see ADV-A-08); the self-financing table can keep growth onboarding explicitly as 'growth cost'
rationale: See ADV-O-11.

claim_challenged: Labour cash is minimised given founder capacity
challenge: The founder takes min(hours, cap) of each role in register order even when coverage or the hire threshold forces employees whose capacity is then idle; freed founder hours are never moved to later roles (implementation, compliance, operations), so idle employees and paid contractors coexist. The coverage optimiser inherits this and undervalues the hire option. Patch (founder takes only hours not absorbed by forced employees) lowers cash by: T1 -$51k (-12%), F1 -$51k, L5 -$51k (-13%), W10 -$58k, L1 -$12k.
evidence: model-p1 patch: fh = min fh0 (max 0 (hours - minEmployees*ProductiveHours)); FOUNDER_ANY=1 run: L5 349,394 vs 400,140; F1 381,332 vs 431,930; W10 444,392 vs 501,970
proposed_change: Allocate founder hours after employee capacity (or solve founder allocation across roles to minimise contract+hire cost, e.g. greedy by contract rate avoided); re-run coverage choice on the reallocated staffing
rationale: Forced employees absorb work before the founder.

claim_challenged: Coverage shortfalls are correctly netted against people already present
challenge: The founder counts as one distinct qualified person in every founder-eligible role at once (management, engineering, operations, compliance) even with zero hours in that role. At F1/T1 the founder's 1,400 h are used up by management and engineering (founder fully utilised at 0 customers), yet the founder is counted as one of the two people for COV-OPS business-day continuity and preparer/reviewer separation. Counting the founder only where they hold hours (on top of ADV-A-06) raises F1/T1 by about $40k (COV-OPS alternative $80k instead of $40k). It also lets one person be on-call primary, change approver, ops preparer and account manager at the same time.
evidence: model-p1 patch (fhRole>0 condition): F1 421,332 vs 381,332 with founder counted everywhere; F n=1 founder hours in operations = 0 in base run
proposed_change: Count the founder toward at most one coverage requirement set (choose the cheapest role to apply them to) and only where the founder holds >= a minimum share of that role's hours; add a Validate rule that founder coverage needs founder hours > 0
rationale: See ADV-P-03.

claim_challenged: Readiness = prepaid annual items newly triggered by customer 1; pre-revenue burn = months x zero-customer cost
challenge: Before the first invoice the business also pays for: first-customer onboarding (ACT-IMP-01 300 h L / 360 h F at $110 = $33-40k), contract counsel (EXP-COR-03 $5k), founder sales time (160 h, displacing about $21k of contract engineering, since the founder is already fully used at 0 customers), and coverage retainers that must exist once customer data is in production (COV-CHG/BRK/ONC $100k/yr, COV-OPS $40k). o0 contains none of these, and readiness counts only Prepaid=Y lines. Under this definition pre-revenue capital is understated by $60-100k+ per model.
evidence: Engine evaluate L n=1 role breakdown (implementation 300 h contract $33k; coverage $100k); capital.csv L base readiness $48.1k = SEC-03/04/05 + INS-01/02/07 only
proposed_change: readiness = (o1 cash - o0 cash for non-recurring onboarding lines and activities) + prepaid lines + go-live share of coverage retainers; or model the pre-revenue months with o1 staffing for the last k months before go-live
rationale: Go-live costs now include first-customer onboarding, acquisition, prepaid items and lead months of run-rate.

claim_challenged: Revised variable cost per account $98 (vs Phase II $147)
challenge: The comparable is (F at 5x2000 - F at 0)/10,000 accounts, so it includes every first-customer step cost (SOC 1/SOC 2 audits, GRC platform, insurance, coverage retainers, monthly-close and auditor-support hours per customer). That is average incremental cost, not variable cost. The actual per-account slope is $65 (1->5x2000), $46 (5->10) and $69 (10->20). The 'revised' variable figure is overstated, which makes the AI-native variable advantage look smaller than the model implies.
proposed_change: Use the slope (F(10)-F(5))/(accounts10-accounts5) or a regression over 5..20 x2000; keep the current figure but label it 'average incremental incl. first-customer step costs'
rationale: Slope between 5 and 10 prior sponsors used.

claim_challenged: $2.5M administration fixed revised to $1.03M; $1.8M licensing fixed revised to $405k
challenge: Scope mismatch: the priors are fixed costs only, but the comparables are total EF cash at 5x2000 including volume-driven labour. Like-for-like is total vs total (prior F $2.5M + $147 x 10,000 = $3.97M vs $1.03M, a 74% cut rather than 59%; prior L $1.8M + $31 x 10,000 = $2.11M vs $405k) or fixed vs fixed (intercept of the zero-based cost line). The table also drops founder labour from 'cash' while the priors priced a salaried CEO/CTO, so only the loaded rows are comparable on management.
evidence: results.md s12; Phase II report 10 ($397 vs $147 vs $31 variable)
proposed_change: Add a 'prior total at 10k accounts' column (fixed + variable x accounts) and compare against EfCash and FullyLoaded; or compare the priors' fixed against the zero-based intercept from a 5->10x2000 regression
rationale: Reports compare prior totals (fixed + variable at 10k accounts: $3.97M administration, $2.11M licensing) with zero-based totals.

claim_challenged: Customer acquisition cost revised from $125k to $24.7k
challenge: (a) EXP-ACQ-01 travel/procurement is tier 3, so it never applies at tier 1 and lineSum 'acquisition' is $0. (b) 160 founder hours are per won customer, with no win rate: at a 25-33% enterprise win rate, lost pursuits triple or quadruple founder time. (c) No marketing, conferences, security-questionnaire engineering hours or pilot concessions. (d) Founder time is priced at $123/h, not the management replacement rate ($144 loaded / $150 contract). A 25% win rate alone gives about $85k.
evidence: explore2.fsx L10 acquisition lines: only EXP-COR-03 $15,000 / 3 new customers; parameters.csv founder_hours_per_new_customer
proposed_change: Reclassify EXP-ACQ-01 as contract-typical (procurement travel is needed to win institutional deals); add param win_rate (0.2/0.33/0.5) dividing founder sales hours and counsel; add security-questionnaire engineering hours per pursuit
rationale: Travel and procurement reclassified as operational; win rate folded into founder hours.

claim_challenged: Registry cost revised from $90-170k to $70.9k
challenge: The comparable omits ACT-PLT-09 'Charity and sanctions data pipeline stewardship' (200 h engineering, about $26k at $130/h), which is the connector maintenance the prior explicitly included (400 h), and omits ACT-SAN-01 sanctions triage. It also prices CHV hours at the founder rate instead of the compliance contract/loaded rate. Adding PLT-09 alone gives about $97k, inside the prior range, so the 'lower than prior' conclusion does not hold.
evidence: explore2.fsx PLT-09 h=200 at F 5x2000; prior-estimates.csv PRI-04 original_assumptions
proposed_change: registry = charity-data lines + (ACT-CHV-* + ACT-SAN-01) hours x compliance contract rate + ACT-PLT-09 hours x engineering contract rate (+ QUAL-03 amortisation in the loaded view)
rationale: Pipeline stewardship included in the registry comparable.

target: Engine.fs:391-393 (SponsorCost); activities.csv sponsor rows; parameters.csv sponsor_staff_rate
claim_challenged: Sponsor-borne cost is reported completely and separately
challenge: Missing sponsor costs: sponsor-side onboarding and migration (data extraction from the incumbent, UAT, parallel run, staff training; ACT-IMP-01 is EF-only and there is no sponsor counterpart), incumbent exit/termination fees, the incremental external financial-audit fee (only staff hours in ACT-AUD-01), and review of SOC reports. sponsor_staff_rate $65/h (Phase II ops rate) is applied to controllers and authorised officers (REC-03 sign-off, GRT-02 decisions, OFAC blocking, AUD-01), who cost $90-150/h loaded. F_system_per_account and the L/W sponsor value proposition (sponsor does exception prep at $65 vs EF ops at $85) are understated.
evidence: headline.csv sponsor_cost (F1 $15.8k, L1 $41.3k); activities.csv has no sponsor onboarding activity
proposed_change: Add sponsor activities ACT-IMP-S (per_new_customer, 200-600 h) and an exit-fee expense; split sponsor rate into sponsor_staff_rate and sponsor_officer_rate ($90/$120/$160) keyed by activity
rationale: Sponsor-side onboarding and migration added; exit fees and sponsor officer rates noted as remaining uncertainty.

claim_challenged: Employees are hired once residual hours exceed 800 because an employee is 'cheaper and more reliable'
challenge: 800 h is far below the cost-neutral point (loaded / contract hourly): engineering 1,512 h, management 1,533, operations 1,423, support 1,303, implementation 1,273, compliance 1,061. Hiring at 801 h costs $196.5k against $104k of contract engineering. With cost-neutral thresholds: L10 -$41k (-8%), L25 -$82k, T5 -$41k, F25 -$77k. If reliability is the reason, it should be stated as a policy premium, not as cheapness.
evidence: hire.fsx with roles thresholds set to loaded/hourly: L10 480,365 vs 521,365; L25 998,039 vs 1,076,316
proposed_change: Set hire_threshold_hours = LoadedAnnual/ContractHourly per role (or make the reliability premium an explicit parameter) and correct the roles.csv wording
rationale: See ADV-O-07.

claim_challenged: Fully loaded C and M include amortised qualification
challenge: The whole DAF platform qualification (ledger, grant lifecycle, sponsor experiences, SOC 2 readiness; 8,360 founder h incl. VAL) is amortised into charity intelligence (C) and migration services (M) as stand-alone businesses: about $232k/yr, so C is $419k loaded at 0 subscribers and M $273k at 0 projects, and C's loaded break-even is 114 subscribers. C needs roughly QUAL-03 + part of QUAL-05. qualAmort also includes VAL-01/02 while capital's qCash excludes them, which is inconsistent.
evidence: results.md s2 C/M at 0 customers; qualification.csv
proposed_change: Add a models column to qualification.csv and amortise only applicable items per model; treat VAL consistently (either in both qCash and qualAmort or in neither)
rationale: Qualification items amortised only to models that need them; validation excluded from amortisation.

claim_challenged: Monte Carlo with 'rho=0.5 adverse-correlated' inputs
challenge: The mixture copula (with probability rho take the common quantile) gives pairwise correlation of about rho^2, measured at 0.28 for rho=0.5, so the label overstates the correlation tested. The MC also holds volumes, mix and prices at base, so the narrow P10-P90 for 'F cash break-even bps at 10' (7.6-9.7) leaves out the mix uncertainty that dominates break-even (ADV-A-02).
evidence: explore2.fsx pairwise corr at rho=0.5: 0.280
proposed_change: Use p = sqrt(rho) for the mixture (or a Gaussian copula with the stated rho) and label as such; add volume factors and a random mix rotation to the MC draws
rationale: Label corrected to describe the common-shock mixture (~0.28 pairwise).

claim_challenged: Low/high columns in capital and prior tables are 'all favourable'/'all adverse' ranges
challenge: These are joint-extreme corners of about 300 ranges set at once (e.g. L capital $76.7k-$1.31M; PRI-01 $206k-$3.65M), with near-zero probability, shown as if they were ranges. The orientation also misses PAR:qualification_amortization_years (high is favourable for loaded, so 'adverse' uses 7 years and lowers loaded cost) and the loaded effect of founder_hours_per_year (1,900 h raises founder noncash in the 'favourable' case).
evidence: Engine.fs:16-18 list; capital.csv low/high rows
proposed_change: Replace oriented corners with MC P10/P90 of the same metrics; add qualification_amortization_years to lowIsAdverse
rationale: Amortisation years and contractor threshold added to adverse orientation; corners kept alongside the Monte Carlo.

target: coverage.csv COV-BRK alt_description; Engine.fs:291 (alternatives priced independently)
claim_challenged: Coverage alternatives are additive and do not overlap with workload contractors
challenge: COV-BRK's own description says the second break-glass holder 'can be the secondary on-call', yet $12k BRK and $36k ONC are both charged. Contracted engineers already paid for 619-1,259 h/yr at L1-L2 are distinct qualified people who could serve as non-author reviewer or secondary on-call, but $100k/yr of retainers (a third of L1 cash) is added on top.
evidence: results.md s4 L1: 1,124 contract hours plus COV-CHG $52k, BRK $12k, ONC $36k
proposed_change: Allow one alternative to satisfy several requirements (a set-cover across alternatives: ONC retainer satisfies BRK); credit a contracted engineer with >= X h/yr as one person toward CHG/ONC
rationale: See ADV-O-15.

target: expenses.csv EXP-SEC-01/02/03, EXP-SUP-01 (fixed); no recruiting/equipment/financial-audit lines
claim_challenged: Expense register is complete
challenge: Headcount-driven costs are missing: seat-priced tools (workspace/identity, code hosting, GRC priced by FTE band, help-desk seats) stay fixed at 0 to 70 employees; there is nothing for recruiting fees (15-25% of salary per hire), equipment or contractor management. There is no financial-statement audit, although AUD-24 ($7k-$50k) is priced in the evidence file and bank-grade sponsors usually ask for vendor financials.
evidence: expense register drivers; data/evidence/prices-ops.csv AUD-24
proposed_change: Add per-employee tooling (Step on employees, needs an Employees metric), recruiting per hire, and EXP-COR-06 financial audit (contract-typical, from 1 customer)
rationale: Per-employee overhead added; a financial-statement audit is not required without lenders or investors.

claim_challenged: Insurance $9.6k/yr at tier 1
challenge: Prices come from micro-SaaS medians (Insureon customers mostly under 5 employees with $50-200k revenue). Underwriting for a vendor that originates payment instructions over $60M-$1.4B of charitable assets (crime/social-engineering, E&O for fund-accounting errors) is likely to be several times higher, and limits of $1-2M are low against a single misdirected grant batch.
evidence: prices-ops.csv INS-01 notes
proposed_change: Widen high ends (e.g. E&O/cyber $10-25k, crime $5-15k) or mark as ASSUMPTION pending broker indication; add a limit-adequacy check versus the largest payment batch
rationale: See ADV-P-15.

claim_challenged: Break-even prices per customer and per account; marginal $/customer
challenge: Per-customer and per-account floors are average cost of the specific mix at n (S, then S+M...), so the n=1-2 floors mostly reflect the S/M identities and perpetual onboarding (ADV-A-05). The 'marginal per customer' column is the cost of whichever profile is next in the pattern plus integer rounding of new customers (Math.Round uses banker's rounding: 1.5->2, 2.5->2, 4.5->4, 7.5->8), so L swings $3.5k / $15.3k / $101k. These are not usable as price guidance.
evidence: price-floors.csv L marginal column; Engine.fs:107
proposed_change: Compute floors on the expected (cycle-average) customer; use average incremental cost over bands (10->25, 25->50) for 'marginal'; use MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero or fractional new customers
rationale: Floors labelled as average cost of the stated mix; marginal reported as band averages in the answers.

claim_challenged: Presentation and units
challenge: Break-even AUA renders as '$1449.00M' / '$20067.00M' (no billions unit). 'never (≤400)' is printed for thresholds searched only to 200. The 'exceptions' metric equals transactions x exception-rate multiplier (2,880 'exceptions' on 2,400 transactions at L1), which reads as an exception count.
evidence: results.md s5/s7; headline.csv L1 row
proposed_change: Add a B unit to money; pass the actual scan limit to optInt; rename the metric to exception_weighted_transactions
rationale: Display corrected.
resulting_change: Render: B unit, scan limits, column rename

claim_challenged: Cash break-even L 7 customers; cash cost is what EF must fund
challenge: The cash view assumes the founder works 1,400 h/yr on the DAF business indefinitely with no draw (noncash $172k/yr, constant at every count). The loaded view adds that but also adds qualification amortisation, so neither view answers 'when can the business pay its founder'. Adding a founder market salary moves L cash break-even from 7 to 8 and widens every pre-break-even deficit by $172k/yr (which also feeds ADV-A-01).
evidence: self-financing.csv L: +$154.6k at 7, +$187k at 8; founder_noncash 172,200 in headline.csv
proposed_change: Add a third view 'cash incl. founder compensation' (EfCash + founder hours x rate) for break-even, self-financing and capital
rationale: Cash-if-founder-paid view added.

claim_challenged: Working capital = collection lag x monthly cost at 1 customer
challenge: Working capital is driven by receivables (lag x monthly revenue), with any shortfall in cost covered by the deficit measure, not by lag x cost. Using o1.EfCash also counts the prepaid annual items already in readiness a second time (about $4k for L). The deficit is not funded anywhere (ADV-A-01), so the WC line is not the binding item.
evidence: capital.csv L base wc $25.5k = 1 x 306k/12
proposed_change: wc = lag x Revenue(1)/12; fund operating losses separately; exclude prepaid lines from the monthly base
rationale: Working capital modelled as first-year collection lag in the growth path.

claim_challenged: Founder labour valued at market rate (fully loaded)
challenge: $123/h is the loaded developer rate (equal to engineering $196.5k/1,600 h), but the founder's first 490-530 h/yr go to management, where the replacement cost is $144/h loaded or $150/h contract. Qualification hours (ledger and fund-accounting design) are also priced at the developer rate. This understates fully loaded cost by about $10-15k/yr, plus the qualification loaded figure.
evidence: roles.csv management loaded 230,000 / 1,600 h; parameters.csv founder_imputed_rate basis
proposed_change: Value founder hours at the replacement rate of the role they fill (role LoadedAnnual/ProductiveHours) rather than a single rate
rationale: The founder substitutes for the scarcest role (engineering); one documented rate keeps the noncash view transparent.
